edges.description: HER2 receptor tyrosine kinase activation drives signaling through the RAS-RAF-MEK-ERK cascade.
HER2 receptor signaling, including ERBB2/ERBB3 dimerization, drives the PI3K-AKT-mTOR cascade.
MAPK signaling drives cell cycle progression
PI3K-AKT signaling cooperates with MAPK to promote neoplastic proliferation and cell survival
Uncontrolled HER2-driven epithelial proliferation produces primary colonic and rectal adenocarcinoma
Intraluminal tumor growth causes mass effect or partial bowel obstruction producing abdominal pain
Mucosal ulceration of proliferating distal colonic or rectal tumors causes lower gastrointestinal bleeding
Chronic occult or overt mucosal blood loss from the colorectal tumor produces iron-deficiency anemia
Progressive tumor burden and systemic cancer catabolism cause unintentional weight loss

nodes.description: Abdominal pain or discomfort from intraluminal tumor mass effect or partial bowel obstruction.

evidence.reference_title: Symptoms and Outcomes in Colorectal Cancer Patients: A Saudi Tertiary Hospital's Five-Year Analysis.
evidence.snippet: The results showed that the most common presenting symptom was abdominal pain (329, 50.2%), followed by weight loss (262, 40%), hematochezia (rectal bleeding or blood in stool) (242, 36.9%), and anemia (238, 36.3%).

nodes.description: Anemia resulting from chronic occult or overt gastrointestinal blood loss from the colorectal tumor.

nodes.description: ERBB2 gene amplification leads to overexpression of the HER2 receptor tyrosine kinase on the cell surface. Amplified HER2 forms homodimers and heterodimers with other ERBB family members (particularly HER3), leading to ligand-independent receptor activation and downstream signaling.

evidence.snippet: Among 5545 patients, 144 (3.1%) had ERBB2 amp+ mCRC.

evidence.reference_title: HER2 in Colorectal Carcinoma: Are We There yet?
evidence.snippet: HER2 (ERBB2) is a member of the ERBB family of receptor tyrosine kinases and functions to drive signaling in the RAS/RAF/MEK/ERK and PI3K/AKT/mTOR pathways.

nodes.description: HER2 receptor activation, including signaling with its dimerization partner HER3 (ERBB3), drives the downstream PI3K/AKT/mTOR signaling pathway in colorectal cancer, promoting cell survival, invasiveness, and resistance to apoptosis.

evidence.snippet: HER2 (ERBB2) is a member of the ERBB family of receptor tyrosine kinases and functions to drive signaling in the RAS/RAF/MEK/ERK and PI3K/AKT/mTOR pathways.

evidence.reference_title: Targeting HER2 in colorectal cancer: The landscape of amplification and short variant mutations in ERBB2 and ERBB3.
evidence.snippet: Mutations affecting HER2 or HER3 can drive downstream processes impacting proliferation and invasiveness and resistance to apoptosis, and have emerged as potential therapy targets.

nodes.description: Antibody-drug conjugate consisting of anti-HER2 antibody linked to topoisomerase I inhibitor payload. DESTINY-CRC01 showed promising activity in HER2-positive metastatic CRC with strong IHC 3+ expression.

evidence.reference_title: Final results of DESTINY-CRC01 investigating trastuzumab deruxtecan in patients with HER2-expressing metastatic colorectal cancer
evidence.snippet: 86 patients were enrolled (53 in cohort A, 15 in cohort B, and 18 in cohort C). Results of the primary analysis are published, reporting an ORR of 45.3% in cohort A.

nodes.description: Dual HER2 blockade with trastuzumab (anti-HER2 antibody) and lapatinib (HER1/HER2 TKI). HERACLES trial demonstrated 30% objective response rate in chemotherapy-refractory, HER2-positive, RAS wild-type metastatic CRC.

evidence.reference_title: Dual-targeted therapy with trastuzumab and lapatinib in treatment-refractory, KRAS codon 12/13 wild-type, HER2-positive metastatic colorectal cancer (HERACLES): a proof-of-concept, multicentre, open-label, phase 2 trial.
evidence.snippet: eight (30%, 95% CI 14-50) of 27 patients had achieved an objective response

nodes.description: Dual HER2 antibody blockade with trastuzumab and pertuzumab, which block different HER2 epitopes and prevent HER2/HER3 heterodimerization. MyPathway basket trial showed activity in HER2-amplified CRC.

evidence.reference_title: Pertuzumab plus trastuzumab for HER2-amplified metastatic colorectal cancer (MyPathway): an updated report from a multicentre, open-label, phase 2a, multiple basket study.
evidence.snippet: one (2%) patient had a complete response and 17 (30%) had partial responses; thus overall 18 of 57 patients achieved an objective response (32%, 95% CI 20-45).

nodes.description: Combination of HER2-selective TKI tucatinib with trastuzumab. MOUNTAINEER trial demonstrated significant activity in HER2-positive metastatic CRC, leading to FDA accelerated approval.

evidence.reference_title: Tucatinib plus trastuzumab for chemotherapy-refractory, HER2-positive, RAS wild-type unresectable or metastatic colorectal cancer (MOUNTAINEER): a multicentre, open-label, phase 2 study.
evidence.snippet: in 84 patients from cohorts A and B in the full analysis set, the confirmed objective response rate per BICR was 38·1% (95% CI 27·7-49·3; three patients had a complete response and 29 had a partial response).
